\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{பங்குச்சந்தை} (paṅkuccantai)}{பங்குச்சந்தை (paṅkuccantai)}]{\ta{பங்குச்சந்தை} (paṅkuccantai) — the stock market}

\label{lesson:TA-C545-pankuccantai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for an omen, then the Tamil for prudence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பங்குச்சந்தை}}
\textbf{\ta{பங்குச்சந்தை}} — \emph{paṅkuccantai} — \textquotedblleft{}the stock market\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{பங்குச்சந்தை} \ta{சரிந்தால்} \ta{பலர்} \ta{பணத்தை} \ta{இழப்பார்கள்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{paṅkuccantai carintāl palar paṇattai iḻappārkaḷ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the stock market falls, many people will lose money.
\end{quote}

Word for word \textquotedblleft{}share market\textquotedblright{}: \ta{பங்கு} \textquotedblleft{}a share\textquotedblright{} + \ta{சந்தை} (\emph{cantai}).

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{பங்குச்சந்தை}} (\emph{paṅkuccantai}) is a modern compound: the native \ta{பங்கு} (\emph{paṅku}), \textquotedblleft{}a share, a portion\textquotedblright{}, from \ta{பகு}, \textquotedblleft{}to divide\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 3808), and \ta{சந்தை} (\emph{cantai}), \textquotedblleft{}a market\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṅkuccantai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṅkuccantai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paṅkuccantai carintāl palar paṇattai iḻappārkaḷ.} — If the stock market falls, many people will lose money.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for an omen, then the Tamil for prudence, then say \emph{paṅkuccantai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{பங்குச்சந்தை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The stock market\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{தரகர்} (tarakar)}{தரகர் (tarakar)}]{\ta{தரகர்} (tarakar) — a broker}

\label{lesson:TA-C545-tarakar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for prudence, then the Tamil for the stock market.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{தரகர்}}
\textbf{\ta{தரகர்}} — \emph{tarakar} — \textquotedblleft{}a broker\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{வீடு} \ta{வாங்க} \ta{ஒரு} \ta{தரகரின்} \ta{உதவியை} \ta{நாடினோம்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vīṭu vāṅka oru tarakariṉ utaviyai nāṭiṉōm.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
To buy a house we sought the help of a broker.
\end{quote}

The fee a broker takes is \ta{தரகு}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{தரகர்}} (\emph{tarakar}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 3090 gives \ta{தரகு} (\emph{taraku}), \textquotedblleft{}brokerage, a middleman's fee\textquotedblright{}, and \ta{தரகன்} (\emph{tarakaṉ}), \textquotedblleft{}a broker\textquotedblright{}; \ta{தரகர்} is the form with the respectful -\ta{அர்}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarakar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tarakar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vīṭu vāṅka oru tarakariṉ utaviyai nāṭiṉōm.} — To buy a house we sought the help of a broker.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for prudence, then the Tamil for the stock market, then say \emph{tarakar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{தரகர்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A broker\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{உயர்த்து} (uyarttu)}{உயர்த்து (uyarttu)}]{\ta{உயர்த்து} (uyarttu) — to lift up; to raise}

\label{lesson:TA-C545-uyarttu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for the stock market, then the Tamil for a broker.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{உயர்த்து}}
\textbf{\ta{உயர்த்து}} — \emph{uyarttu} — \textquotedblleft{}to lift up; to raise\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{கடைக்காரர்} \ta{அரிசியின்} \ta{விலையை} \ta{உயர்த்தினார்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kaṭaikkārar ariciyiṉ vilaiyai uyarttiṉār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper raised the price of rice.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{உயர்த்தினேன்}, \emph{uyarttiṉēṉ}.

The strong partner of \ta{உயர்}, to rise: \ta{விலை} \ta{உயர்ந்தது}, the price rose; \ta{விலையை} \ta{உயர்த்தினார்}, he raised the price.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{உயர்த்து}} (\emph{uyarttu}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 646 gives \ta{உயர்} (\emph{uyar}), \textquotedblleft{}to rise, to be high\textquotedblright{}, and its causative \ta{உயர்த்து}, \textquotedblleft{}to raise\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uyarttu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uyarttu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭaikkārar ariciyiṉ vilaiyai uyarttiṉār.} — The shopkeeper raised the price of rice.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for the stock market, then the Tamil for a broker, then say \emph{uyarttu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{உயர்த்து} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To lift up; to raise\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{கணிசமாக} (kaṇicamāka)}{கணிசமாக (kaṇicamāka)}]{\ta{கணிசமாக} (kaṇicamāka) — considerably}

\label{lesson:TA-C545-kanicamaka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a broker, then the Tamil for to lift up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{கணிசமாக}}
\textbf{\ta{கணிசமாக}} — \emph{kaṇicamāka} — \textquotedblleft{}considerably\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{இந்த} \ta{ஆண்டு} \ta{விற்பனை} \ta{கணிசமாக} \ta{அதிகரித்தது}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{inta āṇṭu viṟpaṉai kaṇicamāka atikarittatu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This year sales went up considerably.
\end{quote}

An adverb in -\ta{ஆக}; before a noun it is \ta{கணிசமான}: \ta{கணிசமான} \ta{தொகை}, a sizeable sum.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \textbf{\ta{கணிசமாக}} (\emph{kaṇicamāka}) is not settled: it is the -\ta{ஆக} adverb of \ta{கணிசம்} (\emph{kaṇicam}), \textquotedblleft{}a considerable amount\textquotedblright{}, whose source is unclear.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṇicamāka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṇicamāka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inta āṇṭu viṟpaṉai kaṇicamāka atikarittatu.} — This year sales went up considerably.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a broker, then the Tamil for to lift up, then say \emph{kaṇicamāka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{கணிசமாக} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Considerably\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{மாதிரி} (mātiri)}{மாதிரி (mātiri)}]{\ta{மாதிரி} (mātiri) — a model; a sample}

\label{lesson:TA-C545-matiri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for to lift up, then the Tamil for considerably.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{மாதிரி}}
\textbf{\ta{மாதிரி}} — \emph{mātiri} — \textquotedblleft{}a model; a sample\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{கடைக்காரர்} \ta{துணியின்} \ta{மாதிரியைக்} \ta{காட்டினார்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kaṭaikkārar tuṇiyiṉ mātiriyaik kāṭṭiṉār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The shopkeeper showed a sample of the cloth.
\end{quote}

In speech it also means \textquotedblleft{}like\textquotedblright{}: \ta{அவனை} \ta{மாதிரி}, like him.

\begin{cousinweb}
The origin of \textbf{\ta{மாதிரி}} (\emph{mātiri}) is not settled: no dictionary we can check gives its source.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mātiri}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mātiri}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaṭaikkārar tuṇiyiṉ mātiriyaik kāṭṭiṉār.} — The shopkeeper showed a sample of the cloth.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for to lift up, then the Tamil for considerably, then say \emph{mātiri} again
\end{itemize}
